```{=html}
<div class="teaching-demo" id="divider-explorer" data-demo="divider" role="region" aria-labelledby="divider-demo-title">
  <div class="demo-heading"><div><p class="demo-eyebrow">Try it · Resistance becomes voltage</p><h3 id="divider-demo-title" class="unnumbered">The ratio sets the reading</h3></div><button type="button" data-fullscreen hidden>Enlarge demo</button></div>
  <p>R1 connects the supply to the output. R2 connects the output to ground. Change either resistor and follow the voltage at their junction.</p>
  <div class="circuit-workbench">
    <div class="circuit-inputs divider-inputs">
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="divider-voltage">Supply voltage (V)</label><input id="divider-voltage-number" type="number" aria-label="Divider supply voltage, volts" min="0" max="12" step="0.1" value="3.3"><input id="divider-voltage" type="range" min="0" max="12" step="0.1" value="3.3"></div>
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="divider-r1">R1 · upper resistor (kΩ)</label><input id="divider-r1-number" type="number" aria-label="R1 upper resistor, kilo-ohms" min="0" max="100" step="0.1" value="10"><input id="divider-r1" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="0.1" value="10"></div>
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="divider-r2">R2 · lower resistor (kΩ)</label><input id="divider-r2-number" type="number" aria-label="R2 lower resistor, kilo-ohms" min="0" max="100" step="0.1" value="10"><input id="divider-r2" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="0.1" value="10"></div>
      <p class="circuit-hint">1 kΩ = 1,000 Ω. Imagine R2 is the photoresistor or thermistor in the next exercise.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="circuit-results">
      <dl class="demo-stats"><div><dt>Output voltage</dt><dd id="divider-output">1.650 V</dd></div><div><dt>Series current</dt><dd id="divider-current">0.165 mA</dd></div><div><dt>Ideal 12-bit ADC</dt><dd id="divider-adc">2048</dd></div></dl>
      <figure class="circuit-figure"><svg id="divider-circuit" viewBox="0 0 600 320" role="img" aria-labelledby="divider-circuit-title divider-circuit-description"><title id="divider-circuit-title">Two-resistor voltage divider</title><desc id="divider-circuit-description">Two 10 kilo-ohm resistors divide 3.3 volts into a 1.65 volt output.</desc><g class="circuit-wire"><path d="M200,40V70 M200,120V160 M200,160V200 M200,250V285 M180,285H220 M186,294H214 M193,303H207 M200,160H375"></path><rect x="182" y="70" width="36" height="50" class="circuit-component"></rect><rect x="182" y="200" width="36" height="50" class="circuit-component"></rect><circle cx="200" cy="40" r="4" class="circuit-node"></circle><circle cx="200" cy="160" r="5" class="circuit-node"></circle><circle cx="375" cy="160" r="4" fill="white"></circle></g><text id="divider-supply-label" x="200" y="24" text-anchor="middle">Vin = 3.3 V</text><text id="divider-r1-label" x="35" y="101">R1 = 10 kΩ</text><text id="divider-r2-label" x="35" y="231">R2 = 10 kΩ</text><text id="divider-output-label" x="395" y="167">1.650 V</text><text x="395" y="137">Vout</text><text x="244" y="292">GND = 0 V</text><text id="divider-top-drop" x="244" y="96">Drop: 1.650 V</text><text id="divider-bottom-drop" x="244" y="226">Drop: 1.650 V</text></svg><figcaption id="divider-ratio">R2 is 50.0% of the total resistance, so Vout is 50.0% of Vin.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="demo-presets" aria-label="Divider experiments"><button type="button" data-divider-preset="10,10">Equal resistors</button><button type="button" data-divider-preset="10,1">Smaller R2</button><button type="button" data-divider-preset="10,100">Larger R2</button><button type="button" data-divider-swap>Swap R1 / R2</button><button type="button" data-divider-double>Double both</button></div>
  <p class="demo-formula" id="divider-formula">Vout = 3.3 × 10 / (10 + 10) = 1.650 V</p>
  <p id="divider-status" class="circuit-status" role="status">The ideal ADC model uses 4,096 equal intervals across 0–3.3 V.</p>
  <details class="demo-explanation"><summary>Why does doubling both resistors keep Vout the same?</summary><p>The fraction R2 / (R1 + R2) stays the same, but total resistance doubles. The series current is therefore halved. If a sensor takes the place of R2, increasing its resistance raises Vout; placing it at R1 reverses that response.</p><p>This model assumes no current is drawn from the output. A load changes the effective lower resistance and the output voltage. A divider is therefore useful for sensing, but it is not a regulated power supply.</p></details>
  <p class="demo-note">The ADC readout uses the same ideal 0–3.3 V model as the <a href="electronics-class-2.html#adc-explorer">ADC explorer</a>. Real ESP32 input range and accuracy depend on hardware, attenuation and calibration. The model's range is not a GPIO voltage rating.</p>
  <div class="demo-footer"><p><strong>Try:</strong> Start with equal resistors. Double both, then swap unequal values. Which readings change?</p><button type="button" data-reset>Reset</button></div>
  <noscript><p>Enable JavaScript to use the controls. With a 3.3 V supply and two 10 kΩ resistors, output is 1.65 V and series current is 0.165 mA.</p></noscript>
</div>
```
